displayedInputs.question: When \(f'(x_0)>0\), how does the tangent line to the curve behave at the corresponding point?

choices.A: It falls from left to right
choices.B: It rises from left to right
choices.D: It has no intersection with the curve

displayedInputs.question: \(f'(x)=2x\). What is the slope of the tangent line to the curve at \(x=-1\)?
If the derivative does not exist, which situation might occur for the tangent line?

choices.A: The slope of the tangent line must be \(0\)
choices.C: The tangent line must pass through the origin
choices.D: The tangent line is perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis, and its slope is undefined

displayedInputs.question: The slope of the tangent line to the curve \(y=x^2\) at the point \((1,1)\) is \(2\). What is the \(y\)-intercept of the tangent line?
What is the slope of the tangent line to the curve \(y=x^2\) at \(x=0\)?
\(f(x)=x^3\), \(f'(x)=3x^2\). What is the slope of the tangent line when \(x=1\)?
When writing the equation of a tangent line, which point must be used in the point-slope form?

choices.B: The origin, regardless of where the point of tangency is
choices.C: Any point unrelated to the curve

displayedInputs.question: What is the value of the derivative function of \(f(x)=x^3\) at \(x=2\)?
Which function is equal to \((x^2)'\)?
What does the derivative of a sum equal?

choices.D: The product of the original two functions

displayedInputs.question: \(y=(2x+1)^2\). What is the derivative at \(x=1\)?
\(y=(3x-1)^2\). What is the derivative at \(x=1\)?
\(f(x)=x^2\) and \(y=f(2x)\). What is the derivative of \(y\) at \(x=1\)?
When differentiating the square of \(ax+b\), what must you also multiply by at the end?

choices.D: The coefficient \(a\) in the inner function

displayedInputs.question: If \(f'(x)>0\) holds throughout an open interval, how does the function behave on this interval?
If \(f'(x)\) is negative on an interval, how does the graph of the function behave from left to right?
\(f'(x)=2x-4\). What is the solution to \(f'(x)>0\)?
\(f(x)=x^2-4x+1\). What is the possible \(x\)-coordinate of a local extremum?
What is the value of \(f(x)=x^2-4x+1\) at \(x=2\)?
For a differentiable function, what is usually true of the derivative at a local extremum?

Suppose \(f\) is continuous at \(c\), differentiable on adjacent intervals \((c-\delta,c)\) and \((c,c+\delta)\) for some \(\delta>0\), and satisfies \(f'(x)>0\) on the left interval and \(f'(x)<0\) on the right interval. What kind of point is \(c\)?
What is the maximum value of \(f(x)=x^2-2x\) on \([0,3]\)?
What is the minimum value of \(f(x)=x^2-2x\) on \([0,3]\)?
For \(f(x)=-x^2+4\) on \([-1,1]\), what is the function value at the endpoint \(x=1\)?
When finding extrema on a closed interval, what else must be compared besides the points where the derivative is \(0\)?

choices.B: Compare only the points where the derivative is \(1\)
choices.D: The two endpoints of the interval

displayedInputs.question: A rectangle has a perimeter of \(20\). Its area is greatest when its length and width are equal. What is this maximum area?
A rectangle has a perimeter of \(20\), with one side of length \(x\) and the other of length \(10-x\). Its area is \(S=x(10-x)\). What is \(x\) when \(S'(x)=0\)?

A rectangle is enclosed with one side along a wall and a total length of 24 meters for the other three sides. The side perpendicular to the wall has length \(x\), and the side parallel to the wall has length \(24-2x\). What is \(x\) when the area is greatest?
What is the final step when using derivatives to solve an optimization problem?

choices.A: Compare the function values at stationary points and at the endpoints of the domain
choices.B: Only set the derivative equal to \(1\)
choices.C: Only consider the length of the domain
choices.D: Replace the function with its derivative and do no further calculations
